channel.title: Bothell & Woodinville Dispatch
channel.description: Bothell & Woodinville news, once a week, from the Bothell & Woodinville Dispatch.

item.title: Both downtowns light their trees Saturday, December 5
item.description: In Bothell, the Northshore Rotary Foundation's festival takes over Main Street at 102nd Avenue NE: a holiday market from noon to 5, activities from 4 to 6:30, and Santa arrives on a Bothell Fire truck to light Lucky the Tree at 5.

item.title: Bothell City Hall is closed today and Friday, and so are the Bothell and Woodinville libraries
item.description: Both libraries reopen Saturday at 11 a.m.; hours by neighborhood below.

item.title: Bothell's 2027–2028 budget is adopted
item.description: The council approved it with the 2027–2033 Capital Facilities Plan last week.

item.title: Woodinville's surface water charge goes from $228 to $235 a year per house in 2027
item.description: It is in the fee schedule that came with the city's 2027–2028 budget, which passed first reading on the November 17 agenda; traffic impact fees rise 3.8% too.

item.title: garbage day slides a day
item.description: If your pickup falls today or later this week, it comes one day late.

item.title: What happens to the parking lot behind the planned six-story building at Main Street and 102nd Avenue NE. The lot stays
item.description: A reader in Downtown Bothell asked what happens to the parking lot behind the planned six-story building at Main Street and 102nd Avenue NE. The lot stays.

item.title: Woodinville is asking what its 1.9 miles of Eastrail should become, and the survey closes Monday
item.description: The corridor runs from Wilmot Gateway Park through downtown to the city limits and would tie into the regional Eastrail, the Sammamish River Trail and the future Centennial Trail extension.

item.title: Bothell's new Downtown Subarea Plan had its public hearing Tuesday; the council is scheduled to decide December 8
item.description: It replaces the 2009 plan with a 20-year plan for downtown and folds four downtown land-use categories into one.

item.title: Bothell's 2027–2028 budget, $479.1 million across all funds, was on Tuesday's agenda for final adoption
Bothell Fire becomes part of the Shoreline Fire Department on March 1, 2027
item.description: Initial results show voters approved Proposition 1; King and Snohomish counties still have to certify.

item.title: the drain on your street
item.description: Leaves on a storm drain grate are how a rainy night turns into water across the street.

item.title: Whether downtown Bothell has enough parking, how the time limits are enforced, and where people who cannot walk far are meant to park
item.description: A reader asked whether downtown Bothell has enough parking, how the time limits are enforced, and where people who cannot walk far are meant to park.
